subject: Computer Networking
title: Modulation Techniques
description: A short lesson to help you apply Modulation Techniques.

hook.text: A radio wave is just a wave. To carry data, you have to change something about it — that's modulation.

buildup.text: AM changes the wave's height. FM changes its frequency. Digital modulation combines both for maximum data density.

discovery.text: QAM — Quadrature Amplitude Modulation — encodes multiple bits per symbol by varying both amplitude and phase.

twist.text: Higher-order QAM packs more bits per symbol but needs a cleaner signal. Noise kills complex modulation schemes.

climax.text: Wi-Fi 6 uses 1024-QAM, encoding 10 bits per symbol. That's why modern Wi-Fi is so much faster than older versions.

punchline.text: Modulation turns waves into data carriers. More complex, more speed.

quiz.question: What does QAM modulate to encode data?
options: Both the amplitude and phase of the signal
Only the frequency of the signal
The physical length of the antenna

details.summary: Modulation techniques encode digital data onto carrier waves using changes in amplitude, frequency, or phase. Advanced methods like QAM combine multiple parameters to pack more bits per symbol. OFDM splits a channel into many subcarriers for robust high-speed transmission used in Wi-Fi and 4G/5G.
details.whyItMatters: Modulation determines how much data wireless systems can transmit within limited spectrum. Better modulation means faster speeds without needing more radio frequencies.
takeaways: QAM encodes multiple bits per symbol using amplitude and phase
OFDM divides channels into subcarriers for reliable throughput
Higher-order modulation requires cleaner signals to decode reliably

faq.question: What is QAM modulation?
faq.answer: Quadrature Amplitude Modulation combines amplitude and phase changes to encode multiple bits per symbol. 64-QAM encodes 6 bits per symbol; 256-QAM encodes 8 bits. Higher-order QAM transmits more data but requires a stronger, cleaner signal. Noise or interference corrupts complex modulation patterns.

faq.question: Why is OFDM important for modern wireless?
faq.answer: Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing splits a wide channel into thousands of narrow subcarriers that transmit in parallel. This resists multipath interference where reflections corrupt signals. OFDM is the foundation of Wi-Fi, 4G LTE, and 5G.
